stem: What does a reconciliation of budgeted profit and actual profit show?

options.content: How each variance moves profit from the budget to the actual figure
options.rationale: Correct: it explains the whole difference.

options.content: The profit to be earned next year
options.rationale: It looks back at the period just ended.

options.content: The cash balance at the end of the period and the bank interest earned
options.rationale: It deals with profit, not cash.

options.content: The amount of tax payable on profit
options.rationale: Tax is not part of a variance reconciliation.

explanation: The statement starts with budgeted profit, adds favourable variances and deducts adverse ones to reach actual profit.

stem: In a reconciliation of standard cost to actual cost, how is an adverse variance treated?

options.content: It is added to the standard cost
options.rationale: Correct: adverse means the actual cost was higher.

options.content: It is deducted from the standard cost
options.rationale: That is how a favourable variance is treated.

options.content: It is ignored because it is a loss
options.rationale: All variances are included to reach the actual cost.

options.content: It is added to the selling price
options.rationale: Variances do not change prices.

explanation: Actual cost = standard cost + adverse variances - favourable variances.

stem: Which term describes investigating only the large variances and leaving normal performance alone?

options.content: Zero-based budgeting method
options.rationale: That is a budgeting approach, not variance investigation.

options.content: Absorption costing
options.rationale: That is a way of valuing products.

options.content: Management by exception
options.rationale: Correct: attention goes to the exceptions.

options.content: Marginal costing
options.rationale: That is a way of valuing products.

explanation: Management by exception saves time by concentrating on significant variances.

stem: A bakery's variance report shows a favourable labour rate variance and an adverse labour efficiency variance. What is the most likely link?

options.content: More skilled workers were used and they were paid more per hour
options.rationale: Higher pay would give an adverse rate variance.

options.content: Cheaper, less experienced workers were used and they took longer
options.rationale: Correct: low-paid workers are often slower.

options.content: The bakery paid overtime to all workers
options.rationale: Overtime raises the rate (adverse).

options.content: The selling price was raised
options.rationale: Selling prices do not affect labour variances.

explanation: A lower grade of worker lowers the rate but may increase the time taken.
hints: Think about who is paid less.

stem: A business switches to a cheaper supplier and shows a favourable material price variance. Which is the most important question to ask before praising the buyer?

options.content: Did the supplier use a larger delivery van to bring the material?
options.rationale: That is irrelevant to the variance.

options.content: Was the standard price written in blue ink?
options.rationale: That is irrelevant.

options.content: Did the cheaper material cause waste or poor quality products?
options.rationale: Correct: the usage variance and quality may offset the saving.

options.content: Did the factory also sell more units?
options.rationale: That belongs to the sales variances, not the link to material price.

explanation: A price saving may be cancelled by adverse usage and efficiency variances or by lost customers.
hints: Cheaper does not always mean better.

stem: Which adverse variance is the production manager least able to control?

options.content: Waste caused by careless cutting of cloth
options.rationale: The production manager controls how carefully work is done.

options.content: Idle time because the workers were not scheduled well by the supervisor
options.rationale: Scheduling is within the manager's control.

options.content: Extra hours worked because of poor supervision
options.rationale: Supervision is within the manager's control.

options.content: A material price rise imposed by all suppliers in the country
options.rationale: Correct: it is outside the manager's control.

explanation: Only a variance with an external cause is uncontrollable; the others arise inside the factory.

stem: After the review of variances, the owner of a furniture workshop sees that overtime has reduced the delivery time but caused adverse labour rate variances. Which factor should she also consider?

options.content: Only the amount of the labour rate variance and nothing else in the report
options.rationale: A financial figure alone ignores the benefit to customers.

options.content: Only the profit of the previous year
options.rationale: Last year's profit does not help decide about overtime now.

options.content: Only the size of the workshop building
options.rationale: Building size is unrelated to the decision.

options.content: The effect of overtime on worker morale and on customer satisfaction
options.rationale: Correct: non-financial factors affect long-term success.

explanation: Cost control should be balanced with morale, safety, quality and delivery.

stem: In a reconciliation of budgeted profit to actual profit, favourable variances are added to budgeted profit.
explanation: True. A favourable variance increases profit, so it is added.

stem: If the reconciliation total does not agree with the actual profit calculated from the actual figures, the most likely explanation is that one or more variances are wrong.
explanation: True. The variances must explain the entire difference, so a mismatch means an error in a variance or an omitted one.
hints: The variances should explain the whole difference.

stem: Match each pair of variances to its most likely common cause.

left.content: Favourable material price and adverse material usage
Adverse sales price and favourable sales volume
Favourable labour rate and adverse labour efficiency
Adverse labour rate and favourable labour efficiency

right.content: Cheaper, poorer quality material that is wasted
A discount given to win extra sales
Lower-paid, less experienced workers who are slow
Highly paid skilled workers who work faster

explanation: Each pair has one cause that moves both variances in opposite directions.
hints: Ask what single decision could cause both.

stem: Complete the formula for actual profit.

payload.template: Actual profit = budgeted profit + {{blank:a}} variances - {{blank:b}} variances.

explanation: Favourable variances add to profit; adverse variances reduce it.

stem: Name the statement that lists variances in columns to move from budgeted profit to actual profit.

accepted.value: reconciliation of budgeted and actual profit

explanation: It is the operating (reconciliation) statement.

stem: A Mutare printer's budgeted profit for May was US\$8,500. The favourable variances were US\$1,150 and US\$350 and the adverse variances were US\$2,050 and US\$590. Calculate the actual profit.
explanation: 8,500 + 1,500 - 2,640 = US\$7,360. Adding the adverse variances instead gives US\$12,640.
workedSolution: 1. 8,500 + 1,500 - 2,640 = US\$7,360. Adding the adverse variances instead gives US\$12,640.
hints: Add favourable and deduct adverse variances.

stem: The standard direct cost of a month's output at a Gweru shoe factory was US\$24,600. The favourable cost variances totalled US\$1,350 and the adverse cost variances totalled US\$2,100. Calculate the actual direct cost.
explanation: 24,600 - 1,350 + 2,100 = US\$25,350. Swapping the signs gives US\$23,850.

stem: A company's budgeted profit was US\$15,000 and its actual profit US\$13,400. The reconciliation shows three variances: sales volume US\$1,700 favourable, sales price US\$2,500 adverse and material usage US\$600 adverse. One more variance is missing from the list. Calculate its amount (state only the amount).
hints: Total variance = actual profit - budgeted profit.

stem: State three actions a manager might take after finding a large adverse material usage variance.

points.description: Investigate the cause (waste, quality, machines, training)
Improve supervision, training or machine maintenance
Change the supplier or tighten quality control of material

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Investigate whether the cause is waste, poor material or faulty machines, then train workers, repair machines or change the supplier.

explanation: One mark for each action.

stem: Explain why a favourable variance may not always be good news.

points.description: It may have been caused by a quality problem, such as cheaper poorer material
It may be linked to an adverse variance elsewhere that is larger
It may show that the standard was too easy or out of date
It may harm customer satisfaction or future sales

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A favourable variance may come from cheaper material that causes waste, which shows up as an adverse usage variance. It may also mean the standard was too loose or that quality and customer satisfaction are suffering.

explanation: One mark for each point.
hints: Think of what else may have changed.

stem: Evaluate whether standard costing variances should be the only measure used to judge a production manager.

points.description: Variances give an objective, quantified measure of cost control
Some variances are outside the manager's control, so judging only on them is unfair
Cost cutting may harm quality, safety, delivery or morale, which variances do not show
Judgement: use variances together with non-financial measures such as quality and on-time delivery

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Variances are objective, but some are outside the manager's control and cost cutting can harm quality and morale. The manager should be judged on variances together with measures such as quality and delivery.

explanation: One mark for each point.

stem: Tatenda Paints in Harare makes paint. The standard for one tin is: selling price US\$30; 2 litres of materials at US\$5.00; 0.5 labour hours at US\$8.00. Budgeted sales were 2,000 tins and budgeted fixed costs US\$12,000. Actual results for the month: 2,150 tins sold at US\$29.00; 4,420 litres of materials bought and used at a total cost of US\$22,984; 1,120 labour hours paid at a total cost of US\$9,184; fixed costs US\$12,300.

parts.label: (b)
parts.explanation: Revenue 62,350 - materials 22,984 - labour 9,184 - fixed costs 12,300 = US\$17,882.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Revenue 62,350 - materials 22,984 - labour 9,184 - fixed costs 12,300 = US\$17,882.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the net total of all the variances (amount only).

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Prepare a reconciliation of budgeted and actual profit with favourable and adverse columns.

points.description: Budgeted profit US\$20,000 at the top
Sales volume US\$2,400 favourable and sales price US\$2,150 adverse
Material price US\$884 adverse and usage US\$600 adverse
Labour rate US\$224 adverse, efficiency US\$360 adverse and fixed cost US\$300 adverse
Totals and actual profit US\$17,882 agree with part (b)

answerSpec.modelAnswer:

| Sales price variance |  | 2,150 |  |

parts.explanation: One mark for each group of lines and one for the agreement with the actual profit.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Comment on the performance for the month.

points.description: Sales volume was above budget but the price cut was larger in effect, so net sales margin fell
All the cost variances were adverse, with material price the largest
Profit was well below budget; the usage and efficiency variances should be investigated and prices reviewed

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: More tins were sold, but the lower selling price cost more than the extra volume gained. All cost variances were adverse, especially material price, so profit fell US\$2,118 below budget. Buying and the price policy should be reviewed.

explanation: This item prepares and interprets a full reconciliation of budgeted and actual profit.
hints: The reconciliation must end at the actual profit.

stem: A Gweru clothing factory has a standard direct cost of US\$52,800 for the month's output. The actual direct cost was US\$54,900. The variance report shows: material price US\$1,350 adverse; material usage US\$900 adverse; labour rate US\$700 favourable; the labour efficiency variance has not yet been calculated.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the total direct cost variance (the amount only).

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the labour efficiency variance (the amount only).

options.content: favourable, because it adds to the cost
options.rationale: A variance that raises cost is adverse.

options.content: adverse, because it adds to the cost
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: favourable, because labour rate is favourable
options.rationale: The two labour variances are independent in sign.

options.content: nil, because it is the balancing figure
options.rationale: It is a balancing figure, but its value is not zero.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Suggest one link between the labour rate and labour efficiency variances.

points.description: The favourable rate suggests lower-paid (less skilled) workers were used
They probably took longer than the standard, giving the adverse efficiency variance

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Lower-paid, less experienced workers were probably used, which lowered the average rate but made the work slower.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Advise the managers which variances to investigate first, giving reasons.

points.description: Material price (US\$1,350) is the largest: check the supplier prices or the standard
Material usage and labour efficiency are controllable inside the factory and may be linked (waste, training)
Investigate before changing workers, because the saving on rate may be cancelled by the time lost

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Start with the largest, the material price variance, to see whether the supplier or the standard is at fault. Then look at usage and efficiency, which the factory controls and which are probably linked to the lower-grade labour.

explanation: This item uses a cost reconciliation to find a missing variance and interpret the pattern.
hints: Total variance = actual cost - standard cost.
